title: Torsion-Sensitive Intermediate Extensions and Prime-Selected Defect Filtrations in Codimension Two
content: Torsion-sensitive Deligne sheaves refine the classical Deligne-sheaf construction by allowing each singular stratum to carry both a truncation degree and a set of retained torsion primes.  We show that, for a rational normal complex surface germ \((X,0)\), this prime-set flexibility organizes the ordinary/dual integral middle-extension defect into a finite prime-selected filtration.  More precisely, the endpoint torsion-retention conditions recover the ordinary and dual middle extensions \(P_{\varnothing}\simeq{}^p j_{!*}\mathbb Z_U[2]\) and \(P_{\mathcal P}\simeq{}^{p^+}j_{!*}\mathbb Z_U[2]\), while every prime condition \(\wp\subseteq\mathcal P(\mathbb Z)\) determines a local defect layer \(E_\wp:=T^\wp E\).  Inclusions \(\wp\subseteq\wp'\) give transition cones \(\operatorname{Cone}(P_\wp\to P_{\wp'})\simeq i_*(E_{\wp'}/E_\wp)\), with the Jung--Saito endpoint comparison as the all-prime case.  Moreover, \(P_\wp\) retains the \(\wp\)-primary torsion on stalks and the complementary \(\wp^c\)-primary torsion on costalks, giving the codimension-two local form of Friedman's complementary-prime duality.  Using the link, exceptional-lattice, and monodromy realizations of \(E\), this filtration becomes computable as \(T^\wp H^2(L,\mathbb Z)_{\mathrm{tors}}\), \(T^\wp(\Lambda^\vee/\Lambda)\), and, in the hypersurface case, \(T^\wp\operatorname{coker}(T-\mathrm{id})_{\mathrm{tors}}\).  Hence, the integral endpoint discrepancy is refined into a functorial system of prime-selected torsion layers, transition defects, and complementary local profiles.
